Canonical 1487–1674 includes grounded special-floor classification, airborne low-Y bypasses, and projected floor/wall checks. The caller at 6276–6283 selects numeric CPU state 4, not a proven death outcome.

The ordered flags and rejection tests match canonical 1522–1565. Angle rejection is strictly greater-than; equality proceeds. The remaining body applies special-line filtering only to floor hits and rejects finite out-of-bound hits with strict comparisons, preserving inclusive accepted boundaries.

Canonical 2643–2754 returns fighter-list members without direct Fighter writes or allocation and forms &fp->cpu before its null guard. gm_16AE 956–988 proves conditional persistent cache writes through the called ranking accessor. Score-standing semantics and portable null tolerance remain appropriately deferred.

The FINAL fact correctly identifies requested player IDs. Canonical 8062–8070 establishes cpu.xC dispatch; 8284–8295 passes 0–3; 7062–7063 forwards the integer; 7014–7023 passes it as player_id; and 2620–2640 compares it with candidate.player_id. It is not an action-mode argument.

Accepted the grounded-caller rejections and retained the related gameplay deferrals. Fighter-directed and destination-directed Y builders do not enforce airborne execution; the explicitly grounded caller contradicts a universal midair-recovery characterization. Brief or sustained Y, directional R, motion names, and numeric action codes do not independently establish short-hop, full-hop, double-jump, air-dodge, ledge outcomes, capture retention, or named moves. The unrestricted integer multiplier permits negative lookahead; conclusions about projection direction require a sign precondition. Stage-prefixed delegates and stored scalar values do not independently prove acid, vehicle, turtle, camera, or other visible hazard semantics, nor transitive purity of their wrappers.

Accepted the item-category, healing-pursuit, named-mode, and rule-mapping deferrals. Exact kind tests, ally-rule calls, target slots, and numeric dispatches are useful retained observations, but do not establish every healing/heavy/hazard/swing/throw category or named CPU mode. Accepted navigation precision deferrals. Directional search suppresses later probes after earlier failures, only midpoint acceptance can initialize the negative sentinel, and the RCruise filter is midpoint-specific. The fighter-target fallback belongs to failed filtered floor queries, not successful queries whose island is rejected. Random-island accumulation and selection use different filters and do not guarantee reachability. The complete current functionality document correctly reconciles shard009 with shard033: the shortfall-derived first operand is an increment capped at 32, while 127 is the separate magnitude clamp. Accepted both upstream clamp-related rejections. Done terminates command execution without neutralizing controller outputs, and available-jump scripts can finish with directional stick intact.

Accepted the non-edge jump and Shrine detour rejections. The non-edge else-if can call the jump builder. Shrine's non-positive-facing branch reverses the vertical subtraction and accepts endpoints at or below current Y; it is not a mirrored upward test. Equality is accepted, and destination preservation/replacement writes XY only.

Accepted the command-consumer deferrals without treating former read-denial notes as evidence of impossibility. Independently read writers now establish fighter-owned serialization and activation for the proposed fact. This does not automatically validate every inherited compound claim about execution outcomes, script-table meanings, charging cancellation, or complete TU gameplay taxonomy. Accepted the action-selection and defensive-input deferrals. Command-7 entry gating has an already-active exception. switch_cmd has an apparent uninitialized source path, so deterministic runtime claims remain deferred. The generic knockback-perpendicular builder has no Nana guard and documents a zero-magnitude uninitialized-output path; numeric motion gates and generated input do not alone prove escape success, maximum DI, shielding, or barrel firing.

The complete current document qualifies shard031's approach wording. ftCo_800A6700 maximizes squared XY separation from the supplied reference among accepted inset endpoints. Nearby-fighter callers submit that result under guards; neither the local approach_pos name nor the 5.0 setter argument proves approach toward the fighter or successful traversal. Accepted all related directional and safety deferrals.

The forwarded integer reaches the candidate.player_id comparison. The inherited compound fact's unresolved disposition is not silently rewritten; the supported correction is supplied by final proposal index8.

Accepted associated-fighter corrections and retained their remaining gameplay/layout deferrals. A void return is not non-returning. History is stored in the receiving fighter's CPU ring and replayed later; correction blends only XY. Exit tests the updated fighter's special-state range, clears left stick/buttons/triggers but not C-stick, and resets the flag on grounded updates rather than only a landing edge. Accepted the scripted-override rejection. The prioritized producer computes environmental classifications from stage, fighter position, blast-zone, and camera observations. It does not read a supplied script command. Detailed delegate gameplay and policy-bit interpretations remain accepted deferrals.

Accepted current input-flow correction and historical-field deferrals. Getter normalization and shared input consumption are independently confirmed, including separate C-stick publication gating and maximum trigger selection. Those narrower checks do not establish old field identities, trigger storage signedness, or compiled offsets, and do not silently promote inherited unresolved compound links.

Missing terminal gameplay consumers, transitive delegate semantics, ranking producers, original-name evidence, complete caller provenance, and external messages remain valid reasons to withhold promotion.
